title: Auto-suggest incident owner based on taxonomy category + impacted service
author: Devon Price
body: Context: As part of the “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping” initiative, we want to reduce paging ambiguity during incident declaration by auto-suggesting a primary owning team/rotation from the selected incident category + impacted service. This PR adds an ownership suggestion engine to incident-bot, a config file that can be maintained without code changes, and safe fallback behavior when inputs are missing/unknown. Summary of changes: 1) New ownership suggestion logic: When declaring or escalating an incident, we compute a suggested owner using the following precedence: (a) impacted_service -> service_owner_map (direct service ownership), else (b) incident_category -> category_owner_map (category-level ownership), else (c) default_owner (SRE on-call). The suggestion is presented as a pre-filled value in the Slack modal (still editable), and is included in the created incident record. 2) Config-driven mapping: Added config/ownership_map.yaml with: service_owner_map (service -> owning_team, rotation, slack_channel), category_owner_map (category -> owning_team, rotation, slack_channel), default_owner, and optional secondary_escalation for a small set of categories (e.g. networking). Config supports a lightweight “aliases” section for service name normalization (e.g. smart-routing vs routing). 3) Fallback + guardrails: If the category is present but not in allowed values (e.g. older taxonomy strings), we log a warning and fall back to category “unknown” -> default_owner. If the impacted service is present but not recognized, we still attempt category mapping and attach “unmapped_service:<value>” as a note in the incident record for later cleanup. If both are missing at declare time, we don’t block declaration; we default owner to SRE and include a modal hint: “Set category/service to improve ownership suggestion.” 4) Feature flag + rollout: Added OWNERSHIP_SUGGESTION_ENABLED (default: true in staging, false in prod) and OWNERSHIP_SUGGESTION_VERBOSE_LOGS (default: false). This lets SRE roll out behind a flag and quickly disable if it causes noise. 5) Tests + telemetry: Unit tests for precedence order, alias normalization, unknown inputs, and YAML validation. Added a counter metric incident_bot.ownership_suggestion.used with tags {source=service|category|default, category=?, service=?} and incident_bot.ownership_suggestion.unmapped_service for reporting on coverage gaps. Implementation notes: The mapping file is intentionally small and meant to be updated as ownership evolves; this PR does not attempt to encode the entire service catalog. The goal is to cover the top incident-driving services and the top taxonomy categories from the reliability program. This PR assumes taxonomy fields are already added to the declare flow (PR #218) and will gracefully degrade if those fields are not present (older commands / partial workflows). Example (from config/ownership_map.yaml): category_owner_map: routing_overload: owning_team: Platform (Routing) rotation: oncall-platform-routing slack_channel: "#eng-platform" capacity_exhaustion: owning_team: Infra (Fleet) rotation: oncall-infra-fleet slack_channel: "#eng-infra" service_owner_map: smart-routing: owning_team: Platform (Routing) rotation: oncall-platform-routing slack_channel: "#eng-platform" gateway-edge: owning_team: Infra (Networking) rotation: oncall-infra-net slack_channel: "#eng-infra" default_owner: owning_team: SRE rotation: oncall-sre-primary slack_channel: "#eng-sre" Screenshots/UX: The “Owner” field in the Slack modal now pre-populates with the suggested rotation (e.g., oncall-platform-routing) and shows a small helper text “Suggested based on category + impacted service”. It remains editable. If the bot falls back to default owner due to missing inputs, helper text changes to “Defaulted to SRE (missing/unknown category or service)”. Follow-ups: - ENG-4825: enforce allowed-values + migration strategy for taxonomy strings so we reduce unknown-category fallbacks. - ENG-4831: use the new metrics to drive monthly ownership map coverage improvements. - Add a small admin command /ownership-map validate to run YAML validation in prod without redeploy (not included here).
commits: incident-bot: add ownership suggestion engine w/ precedence rules
config: introduce ownership_map.yaml w/ service + category maps and aliases
slack: prefill Owner field and add helper text + fallback messaging
metrics: emit ownership suggestion source + unmapped_service counters
tests: YAML validation, alias normalization, precedence + fallback cases
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Love the precedence order. Can we ensure declare does not hard-fail if taxonomy fields are missing? We still have a few older /incident declare paths in use.

Devon Price (author): Yep — declare continues to accept missing fields. In that case we suggest default_owner and add helper text. Added a test for missing category+service and verified no modal validation errors.

Irene Choi (review): For capacity-related categories, we should prefer Infra/Fleet even if service is unknown. Looks like you’re doing category fallback; 👍. Can we add a secondary escalation channel for Networking when impacted_service is gateway-edge?

Devon Price (author): Added optional secondary_escalation in YAML. For gateway-edge service mapping, primary is oncall-infra-net, secondary is #eng-sre for IC coordination. Let me know if you’d prefer #eng-platform for edge, but I matched current on-call routes.
Mina Haddad (review): Minor: can we normalize “smart routing” and “smart-routing” and “routing” to avoid missing service map? Some teams use different strings.
Devon Price (author): Added aliases list for smart-routing + routing. Also added metric incident_bot.ownership_suggestion.unmapped_service so we can see what else to alias post-rollout.

Dev Patel (review): From Support POV, if Owner defaults to SRE due to unknown category, can we include a note in the incident record that the service string was unmapped? This will help us fix tickets like SUP-1842 faster.
Devon Price (author): Added note unmapped_service:<value> to the incident record when we see an unrecognized service. Also emitting a counter with the raw value for quick reporting.

Miles Thornton (review): Config looks good. Please keep taxonomy keys aligned with v1 naming (snake_case). I see routing_overload/capacity_exhaustion; matches draft. Can we add a comment header in YAML pointing to the Confluence spec once it lands?
Devon Price (author): Added header comment with placeholder link + ENG-4823 reference. We can update to final Confluence URL after publish.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Please coordinate rollout flag flip with #eng-releases once merged.
Devon Price (author): Will do — I’ll ship to staging with flag enabled, then request a short prod enable window for SRE to monitor metrics.
